raw_response:
I will not start from zero. On my land in Quzhou, the main income is still wheat-maize, so I will keep most of the 19.1 mu in that rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I have done this many years, and with well water in hand I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard, because if yield falls, that loss is bigger than wasting a little fertilizer. I studied through middle school, so I do look at soil strength, water, and what the local dealers and other farmers are doing, but I still trust what has worked on fields like mine. This year I will put 15.1 mu into winter wheat and then summer maize on the same 15.1 mu, and I will keep 4.0 mu in cotton. For wheat, I will push for a steady stand and good ears, so I will use improved seed, enough nitrogen to hold yield, phosphorus for rooting, a little potassium, three irrigations, and three pesticide passes. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into hybrid maize on the same ground with no-tillage or very light disturbance, because time is tight and that saves labor; maize will get solid nitrogen, some phosphorus and potassium, two irrigations, and two sprays. Cotton I will keep on the smaller block because it needs more watching and labor; I will still feed it well, irrigate three times, and spray more often because insects can ruin cotton fast.
